# Python-semantics traps in Rust ports

Every one of these produced a confirmed parity defect during the v14 P2 ports (found by codex finder passes with reproduced counterexamples). Check each when porting or reviewing.

1. **str whitespace sets differ.** Python `str.strip()`/`split()`/`isspace()` treat `\x1c`–`\x1f` (FS/GS/RS/US), `\x85`, and more as whitespace; Rust `trim()`/`split_whitespace()` (Unicode White_Space) do not. Bit activity twice and buckets once. Use the shared core py-whitespace helper — never raw `trim()`/`split_whitespace()` where Python parity matters.
2. **Duplicate JSON object keys.** Python `json.loads`/orjson keep the LAST occurrence (by decoded key); sonic-rs preserves duplicates and field lookup returns the FIRST. Bit ids, activity, and all three smallmods ports. Use the shared last-wins value accessor for any object field read that mirrors Python dict semantics.
3. **Float formatting ties.** Rust `format!("{:e}")`/`{}`/plain Ryū are NOT ECMAScript/Python-repr tie-exact (counterexample: 698957826421429.2). Use `ryu-js`; fuzz new formatting paths against Python. Python `round()` is half-even.
4. **Value preservation over type-filtering.** Python stores whatever the JSON carried (`replace_all=1` stays `1`; `content: 7` becomes `str(7)`="7" where Python str()-coerces — mirror the exact Python op, neither reject nor silently empty). Bit toolcall and notifications.
5. **Materialization drops.** The Python parse path drops events whose timestamps can't materialize. Rust paths consuming `parse_bytes` directly must apply the same drops. Bit activity_lift. (P3 moves the guard to parse time.)
6. **Code-point vs byte string ops.** Python slicing/truncation is code-point-based.
7. **Big integers.** Python ints are arbitrary precision AND Python's `/` is true division on ints (exact); Rust f64-cast-then-divide loses ulps on huge counts (bit cost: 9_007_199_254_740_993 tokens). Mirror Python's division order; project big ints via int-from-string (see digest doc 35f43592).
8. **Regex engine dialect ≠ pattern bytes.** A generated pattern can be byte-identical in Python `re` and Rust `regex` yet match differently: `\s` (Python includes \x1c-\x1f), `\w`/`\b` (combining marks, İ). Bit buckets' junk pattern. See the rust-regex-dialect-parity doc (d458ca8) for the established convention; when a class diverges, expand it explicitly in the generated pattern and pin the divergent inputs in the golden.
9. **Timestamp precision.** Python datetime is MICROSECOND precision — sub-µs digits truncate at parse; chrono keeps nanoseconds, changing sort order of near-tie events (bit buckets). Truncate to µs at the shared timestamp-parse owner (core parse.rs), not per-consumer.
10. **Lenient shape fallbacks.** Python `.get()` chains fall back silently (null flat field ignored when the per-TTL split exists; `{}` falls back to flat; floats priced); Rust `require_*` helpers reject. Mirror the exact Python access pattern per field (bit cost's usage adapter).
